instrucciones: 4. READ this conversation and COMPLETE your part. Write the numbers (1-6) and complete each sentence on your exam paper. (1.5 points) If a gap ends with a question mark, you must write a question.

instrucciones: 5. Choose ONLY 3 of the following situations and WRITE what you would say in each one to show that you understand the context of the situation. Write between 10 and 25 words. (1.5 points) Only the first three you answer will be marked.

items.enunciado: a) Your friend says, “Buying clothes online is always cheaper than buying them in a shop.” Give your opinion.
items.modelo: I’m not sure I agree. Online prices can be low, but you often have to pay for delivery, and returning clothes can be annoying.
criterios: Lo que escribo encaja con la situación o con la conversación (si el hueco acaba en «?», es una pregunta).

Ni muy corto ni muy largo: en las situaciones, entre 10 y 25 palabras.
items.explicacion: Dar una opinión: «I’m not sure I agree / I think…» con una razón concreta. 10–25 palabras.

items.enunciado: b) The trainers you ordered online arrived two weeks late and the box is damaged. Complain to the customer service worker.
items.modelo: Hello, my trainers arrived two weeks late and the box was damaged. I’m very disappointed, so I would like a refund, please.

Ni muy corto ni muy largo: en las situaciones, entre 10 y 25 palabras.
items.explicacion: Quejarse: exponer el problema («arrived late», «damaged»), mostrar disgusto y pedir una solución con educación.

items.enunciado: c) Your younger cousin wants to buy a video game with his parents’ credit card without asking them. Advise him.
items.modelo: If I were you, I would ask your parents first. Using their card without permission could cause a big problem at home.
criterios: Lo que escribo encaja con la situación o con la conversación (si el hueco acaba en «?», es una pregunta).

items.explicacion: Aconsejar: «If I were you, I would… / You should… / You’d better…» y una razón.

items.enunciado: d) A classmate asks you to lend him money to buy a jacket online. You don’t want to. Refuse politely.
items.modelo: I’m sorry, but I’d rather not lend money to anyone. Why don’t you wait for the sales? The jacket might be cheaper soon.

titulo: The school where plastic is not allowed
instrucciones: Read the text and answer questions 1, 2 and 3. In question 1, copy the exact words from the text as evidence; in question 2, copy no more than 10 words; in question 3, find the word in the text that matches each definition.
texto:
At Hillcrest Secondary School, the canteen no longer sells anything wrapped in plastic. Since September, students have been drinking from metal bottles, eating lunch from reusable boxes and carrying their books in cloth bags. The change began with Marta Quintero, a science teacher who was shocked by the amount of rubbish her classes produced in a single week.

“We counted more than two thousand plastic items in five days,” Marta says. “Most of them were used for ten minutes and then thrown away.” After sharing the results with the headteacher, she formed a student committee of twelve members. They visited local shops, asked for advice from an environmental group and wrote a plan for the whole school year. The school now provides water fountains in every corridor, and the canteen buys fruit and sandwiches from a bakery that uses paper packaging.

Not all students were happy at first. Some complained that reusable boxes were heavy and difficult to clean, and a few parents worried that healthy snacks would cost more. However, the committee found that the opposite was true. Families spend less on drinks and wrapping, and the canteen has reduced its monthly bill by almost a fifth. “I was sceptical,” admits Luis, a fifteen-year-old student. “Now I forget my bottle and feel strange without it.”

The project has also changed how students see their daily habits. Every Friday, volunteers collect any plastic found in the playground and turn it into art for the main hall. Marta believes this is the most valuable result of the scheme. “We wanted to reduce waste,” she says. “What we did not expect was to see younger children teaching their parents to recycle.” Other schools in the region are now asking to visit Hillcrest, and the local council is studying whether to offer similar help to ten more centres next year.

items.pregunta: 1. Say whether the following sentences are TRUE or FALSE according to the text. COPY the evidence from the text. No marks will be given without the evidence. (1.5 points)

items.afirmacion: b) The student committee asked an environmental group for help.
pruebas: asked for advice from an environmental group
They visited local shops, asked for advice from an environmental group
items.explicacion: TRUE: el comité pidió consejo a un grupo ecologista («asked for advice from an environmental group»).

items.afirmacion: c) The canteen has spent more money since the changes began.
pruebas: the canteen has reduced its monthly bill by almost a fifth
Families spend less on drinks and wrapping
items.explicacion: FALSE: la cantina ha reducido su factura mensual casi una quinta parte, así que gasta menos, no más.

instrucciones: 6. Choose ONE of the following topics and WRITE a composition of about 140-180 words. If you choose the email, DO NOT SIGN it. (3 points)

items.enunciado: a) Should schools ban single-use plastic completely? Give your opinion.
items.modelo:
Every day, schools throw away thousands of plastic bottles, wrappers and cups, so the idea of banning single-use plastic is becoming more and more popular. In my opinion, schools should ban it, although it will not be easy at the beginning.

First of all, a plastic-free school sets a good example. Students spend many hours there, and what they see every day shapes their habits. If they learn to use a metal bottle and a lunch box, they will probably do the same at home. Moreover, schools can save money in the long run, because they will not need to buy so many disposable products.

However, some people say that a total ban is unrealistic. Reusable bottles are expensive for some families, and the canteen may need new equipment. For this reason, the school should offer help, for example free water fountains or a second-hand bottle shop.

In conclusion, I believe a plastic-free school is a small change that can have a big effect on the planet and on our daily habits.
criterios: Presentación: párrafos claros, puntuación correcta.
Organización: estructura del tipo de texto (email; for & against; opinion essay), registro adecuado, ideas enlazadas con conectores.
Contenido: me ciño al tema, ideas suficientes y variadas, sin repeticiones.
Corrección gramatical: frases bien construidas, variedad de estructuras, sin traducir del español.
Vocabulario: rico y no copiado del texto; menos de 4 faltas de ortografía (más de 3 restan).
items.explicacion: Opinion essay: introducción con la postura, un párrafo por idea con conectores (first of all, moreover, however, in conclusion), reconocer el argumento contrario y conclusión. Entre 140 y 180 palabras: por debajo de 140 baja el tope de nota.

items.enunciado: b) Write an email to a friend from another school telling him or her about the plastic-free week at your school and asking him or her to start a similar project at his or her school.
items.modelo:
Hi Lucas,

How are things going? I hope you are enjoying the new school year. I’m writing to tell you about something exciting that happened at my school last week.

We had a “plastic-free week”, and everybody took part. Students brought water in reusable bottles and snacks in lunch boxes instead of plastic bags. In the canteen, there were no disposable cups or straws, and the teachers even used paper instead of plastic folders. At the end of the week, we counted the rubbish and we had thrown away about 70% less plastic than usual. We were really surprised!

The best thing was that it was not difficult, and it made us think about how much we waste. Now the headteacher wants to continue the project all year.

Why don’t you try something similar at your school? You could start by talking to your teachers and your classmates. I’m sure they will like the idea, and I can send you some of our posters if you want.

Write soon and tell me what you think.

Best wishes,

Organización: estructura del tipo de texto (email; for & against; opinion essay), registro adecuado, ideas enlazadas con conectores.
Contenido: me ciño al tema, ideas suficientes y variadas, sin repeticiones.
Corrección gramatical: frases bien construidas, variedad de estructuras, sin traducir del español.
Vocabulario: rico y no copiado del texto; menos de 4 faltas de ortografía (más de 3 restan).
